description: Stock male AI narration for a fictional classroom case. No voice cloning.

scenes.label: The first report
scenes.text: At six ten this morning, a resident on the third floor of The Halden heard a loud crack. They found a new diagonal crack running across the hallway wall and into the ceiling near the east stairwell. The overnight security contractor called nine one one.

scenes.label: Evacuation
scenes.text: Half an hour later, at six forty, the Cincinnati Fire Department ordered a precautionary evacuation. All two hundred and thirty-six residents are out of the building. Nobody is hurt. The cause of the crack is still unknown.

scenes.label: The inspection
scenes.text: It is now eight oh five. A city structural inspector is due to arrive at nine this morning. Nobody may go back inside, even to collect belongings, until the inspector permits it. There is no confirmed time for residents to return.

scenes.label: Residents
scenes.text: It is thirty-eight degrees Fahrenheit and raining. Most residents are sheltering in the lobby and parking garage of the building next door, which Tallgrass does not own. Others have gone to friends' apartments. Many left without coats, laptops, medications, or car keys. Final exams begin in three weeks.

scenes.label: Who is available
scenes.text: Property manager Marcus Reyes is on site. Kessler-Brandt Construction and Larkin and Pell Structural Engineers have been called, but neither has called back. Chief executive Dana Whitlock has been told about the evacuation. She is returning from Columbus and is reachable by phone.

scenes.label: Public attention
scenes.text: A resident posted a video of the crack at six fifty. It already has forty thousand views. The residents' group chat has one hundred and ninety members and is moving quickly. Two parents have called the leasing office, which opens at nine. Tallgrass has said nothing publicly so far.

scenes.label: The reporter
scenes.text: In an email received at seven fifty-two, Channel Seven reporter Priya Natarajan asks what caused the evacuation, whether anyone was hurt, when residents can return, and how Tallgrass is helping. She wants a statement by nine for the website and noon news. She also invites someone to speak on camera at eleven.

scenes.label: Your first response
scenes.text: Read the full update below, then discuss your first response. Start the situation summary, holding statement, and message to your priority stakeholder on the paper memo handout. Decide who will speak for the company and what it should do now. Record your first decision and reasoning in section seven.

scenes.label: Tonight
scenes.text: It is now nine ten, and the inspector is inside the building. The fire department has unofficially told Marcus Reyes that The Halden will remain closed at least through tonight. A plan is needed for where two hundred and thirty-six students will sleep.

scenes.label: Claims online
scenes.text: A post from eight forty-one claims The Halden is condemned and collapsing, two students are hospitalized, and Tallgrass knew. It has twelve thousand shares. The account has three hundred followers and no connection your team can identify. Your team's information says the building was evacuated, not condemned, and nobody has been hospitalized.

scenes.label: Earlier requests
scenes.text: Maintenance screenshots from the residents' chat are circulating on TikTok and X. On October twenty-eighth, Unit three twelve reported new hallway cracks. That request was closed the next day. On November third, Unit three eighteen reported a longer crack and a sticking door. It was closed that day. Both were marked cosmetic, with no action required.

scenes.label: A third request
scenes.text: On November tenth, Unit three twelve submitted another request. The resident said this was the third time, the crack now reached the ceiling, and someone needed to look at it. The request was closed the next day as cosmetic. All three requests were closed within a day, from Marcus Reyes's account.

scenes.label: Parents’ calls
scenes.text: Since nine this morning, the leasing office has received forty-four calls from parents. A mother in Dayton posted on Facebook that she is driving down to get her daughter and nobody from the company will answer. Other parents ask about rent refunds and ending leases. The supplied lease terms are in the company resources.

scenes.label: The reporter
scenes.text: Priya Natarajan now has the maintenance screenshots. She asks whether Tallgrass ignored warnings about the wall for three weeks. She also asks again whether someone will go on camera at eleven. Your team needs to discuss that interview request alongside the other decisions in this update.

scenes.label: The callback
scenes.text: Kessler-Brandt Construction has called back. Its only response is that it will be reviewing the matter with counsel. Larkin and Pell Structural Engineers has still not returned the company's calls.

scenes.label: Revisit your memo
scenes.text: Read the full update, then revisit your paper memo. Review the situation summary, holding statement, stakeholder message, and actions for the next twenty-four hours. Discuss the interview request. In the Update Two row of section seven, record what your team decided and what changed your thinking.

scenes.label: The finding
scenes.text: At eleven fifteen, the inspector issues a preliminary finding: a failed steel connection at a third-floor transfer beam. The building is unsafe to occupy until temporary shoring is installed and a full structural review is complete, a minimum of ten to fourteen days. Escorted fifteen-minute visits to retrieve essential belongings will begin on Wednesday.

scenes.label: Two statements
scenes.text: Two organizations have issued statements to Channel Seven. At eleven oh five, Kessler-Brandt says it built to the engineer's drawings, passed every city inspection, and is confident in its work. At eleven twenty, Larkin and Pell says its design was sound and it is reviewing whether construction matched that design. These are the organizations' accounts.

scenes.label: The university
scenes.text: In a statement issued at ten fifty, the University of Cincinnati says The Halden is privately owned and operated and is not affiliated with the university. Student Affairs is helping affected students with information about temporary housing.

scenes.label: An earlier warning
scenes.text: Former maintenance technician Tom Delgado has spoken to Priya on camera. He says he flagged out-of-square door frames on the third floor in August and was told it was normal settling. Delgado left Tallgrass in September. This is his account of that earlier concern.

scenes.label: The chief executive
scenes.text: It is now eleven thirty, and Dana Whitlock has arrived. She wants to issue a statement within the hour blaming the contractor. Her proposed wording says that Tallgrass was as surprised as anyone. She wants your team's recommendation in writing.

scenes.label: Help available
scenes.text: A local hotel group has offered one hundred and twenty rooms at a reduced rate for two weeks. The nightly rate is not given. UC's Campus Recreation Center has opened as a daytime warming space for residents. The company's spending authority and lease terms remain available in the company resources.

scenes.label: A planned protest
scenes.text: In their group chat, residents are organizing a protest outside the leasing office for five o'clock this afternoon.

scenes.label: Your final response
scenes.text: Read the full update and finish all seven sections of your paper memo, including the public statement, advice to the chief executive, stakeholder message, and three immediate actions. Record your latest decision in section seven. Prepare your two-minute briefing. Keep the memo for the debrief, then hand in one completed paper memo per team at the end of class.
